pics.alt: Title page of the 1798 first edition of An Essay on the Principle of Population
pics.caption: Title page of the first edition of Thomas Robert Malthus's An Essay on the Principle of Population (London: J. Johnson, 1798), published anonymously. Its contrast between geometric growth of population and arithmetic growth of subsistence motivated the logistic models of Verhulst and later demographers.

pics.alt: Early twentieth-century table of the thorium, actinium and radium decay series with half-lives and radiations
pics.caption: Table of the thorium, actinium and radium decay series after Ernest Rutherford, from Popular Science Monthly, volume 73 (1908), listing each product's time to be half transformed (its half-life) and its radiations. The values reflect the knowledge of the time; radium's half-life, given here as 1,200 years, is now known to be about 1,600 years.
